reads.label: Country-report register (pos); collective first-person ' we' (neg, sharp but small)
reads.summary: Mostly-positive neuron whose positive pole tracks country-fact-sheet / human-rights-report register, and whose sparse negative pole is a very sharp, low-magnitude response to the token ' we', especially in national first-person-plural constructions ('In China, we have provided...').

positive.read: Fires on section-head and fact-sheet tokens in country-profile documents: ' Contents', ' Labor' (Child Labor), ' Profile' (Country Profile), ' freedom', ' government', ' est' (pop. est.), plus ' multiparty', ' unicameral'. Source docs are World-Factbook-style country pages, human-rights reports, and 'Country ah:' fact quizzes (Ukraine, India).
evidence: act 8.06 on ' Contents' in a Uganda table-of-contents page (d1207); 4.03/3.69 on ' Labor' in Child Labor reports (d4758); 3.66 on ' Profile' in 'Zimbabwe Country Profile 2015' (d3558).
Full pass 2: top token ',' share 0.086 at lift 2.22 over 22,396 fires in 1,767 docs - broadly selective, register-level rather than token-level.

negative.read: Sharp ' we' response: ' we' is 45.1% of negative-pole sparse fires at 200x lift over ~4.4 effective token types, at small magnitude (min act -0.78). Contexts are national collective statements: 'In China, we have provided...', 'In Canada, we tend to...', 'we will withdraw our combat troops'.
evidence: ' we' x9 of 32 exemplars, lift 199.99, eff_tokens 4.4; 853 fires across 485 docs.
d3222 'In China, we have provided...' (act -0.78); d4466 'In Canada, we tend to...' (act -0.59).

caveats: Negative-pole magnitude is ~10x smaller than positive (min -0.78 vs max 8.06); treat the ' we' pole as weak/suppressive (neg q9999 = 0.269).
Single latent with 67 attribution fires - low independent support.
validation: Wrong-context control: ' we' in non-national contexts vs 'In <country>, we...' frames.
Compare against magnitude-matched same-layer controls on country-report pages.

reads.label: Comics-creator credit lines (pos) vs franchise/superhero titles (neg)
reads.summary: Pop-culture/fandom neuron. Positive pole fires on comic-creator surnames inside writer/artist credit lines; negative pole on superhero-franchise and media-title tokens. Both poles live in the same fandom register, so the split looks like creator-byline context vs franchise-title context.

positive.read: Credit-line onomastics: ' Cates', ' Brisson', ' Larsen' x2, ' Quitely', ' Pak', ' Turner', ' Aaron', ' Lemire', ' Prophet', ' House', ' ant' (Arrant) - nearly every exemplar is adjacent to 'Writer:', 'Artist:', 'Colorist:', 'Letterer:' or comic-news prose.
evidence: act 8.06 'Writer: Donny C[ates]' (d4003); 7.88 'Ed Bris[son]' (d4003); 6.78/6.53 'Erik Lars[en]' (d1086 x2).
6.69 'a touch of Frank Quit[ely]' (d499); 6.25 'comic scripts for Michael [Turner]'s Fathom' (d3402).

negative.read: Franchise/title tokens: 'UE' (JUSTICE LEAGUE), 'JL', 'aways' (Runaways), 'Corp' (LexCorp), 'vel' (Captain Marvel) x2, 'OR' (THOR), 'girl' (supergirl), ' Jones' (Jessica Jones), '#' in series numbering - acts -0.33 to -0.59.
evidence: act -0.59 'JUSTICE LE AG[UE]' (d4451); -0.42 'developing it for Lex[Corp]' (d36); -0.37 'Netflix has nothing to compare with... Jessica [Jones]' (d3015).
Full pass NEG: only 327 fires; ' series' lift 450x on share 0.061 - thin support.

caveats: Negative sparse-tier support is thin (n_fire 327).
Both poles share the comics register; the byline-vs-title split needs controls.
validation: Creator names in non-credit prose vs credit-line positions.
Franchise tokens inside byline documents vs standalone fan prose.

reads.label: Language discriminator: Turkish strongly negative, Hungarian weakly positive
reads.summary: The huge-magnitude pole is negative on Turkish text (acts to -15.4, neg q9999 = 4.57) while the weak positive pole fires on Hungarian fragments - a language-identification signal in an early MLP layer, not the ','-token detector the dossier's provisional read describes.

positive.read: Hungarian tokens and morphology: 'o-umlaut' fragments in Angyalfold, 'ede' (gyujtemeny), 'inc' (Kazinczy), 'res' (Weores), 'old', 'av' - language-renewal, Budapest placename and translated-casino fragments.
evidence: act 0.77 on 'o-umlaut' in 'Angyalf[oe]ld' (d2030 x2); 0.51 'Ferenc Kazinczy... language renewal' (d1158).
Full pass POS: ',' share 0.214, lift 5.52, eff 12.2 over only 327 fires - small-n tail.

negative.read: Turkish byte-fragments across news, recipes, academic and travel text: 'uden' (Oludeniz), 'ru' (Dogru), 'im' (Anabilim), 'y' (Biyokimya), 'ok', 'k' (Anitkabir), 'sal' (Unsal), 'akk' (Canakkale), 'iant' (Gaziantep) at acts -9.6 to -15.4.
evidence: act -15.38 'Ol[uden]iz' (d2400); -12.88 'Dog[ru]' in an author list (d2010); -10.31 'Onur with Turkish under-secretary context' (d4410).
Full pass NEG: 16,780 fires over 1,790 docs, neg q9999 = 4.573 - the dominant pole.

caveats: Positive pole is small-magnitude (max 0.77) - Hungarian support is weak relative to the Turkish signal.
Attribution rests on 2 latents (~390 fires each).
validation: Score clean Turkish vs Hungarian vs matched Latin-script controls (Romanian, Azerbaijani).
Check whether ',' selectivity survives a language control.

record.summary: Weather-numeracy neuron. Positive pole fires on integer temperature values in casual forecast/observation contexts (deg F highs); negative pole on meteorological-instrument and precipitation jargon and on metric/scientific temperature notation (Celsius, Kelvin, mm).

pos.reading: Numerals as temperatures: '68'/'67 degrees' in TV weather transcripts (act 10.1/7.4), '75 to 80', 'high near 54 F', 'the 60s/70s', 'Highs just kiss 80' - tail-hist 60x5, 70x3, 80x3, 68x2, 75x2, 50x2 plus ' degree'.
evidence: act 10.06 'washington. [68] down town. 57 in fairfax' (d939); 7.44 'a cool, comfortable [67] degrees' (d2991).
7.06 'Temperatures are expected to reach the [60]s' (d3206); 5.94 'growing [degree] days > 50 F' (d1456).

neg.reading: 'Surface' (Surface Map), ' pressure' x2, ' light' rain x3, ' showers', 'barometric' fragment, ' inches', ' mm', ' frost', plus decimals in Kelvin/Celsius/pressure readings ('273.00 K', '[38] C', '30.[05] falling').
evidence: act -3.05 '[Surface] Map 11 AM: High pressure settling' (d4536); -2.16 '273.[00] K' (d674); -2.05 'one August at [38] C' (d3489).
-2.11 'on 99[mm] for the 4 days' (d20); -2.08 'humidity and bar[ometric] pressure' (d3069).

caveats: Full pass shows broad selectivity both poles (eff 125/99) - the numeral story is exemplar-tail (strongest-case) behavior.
The F-vs-metric negative sub-pattern is secondary; a few negative exemplars are plain weather words.
validation: Same numerals in temperature vs non-temperature contexts (addresses, scores).
Direct deg-F vs deg-C notation comparison.

The negative pole fires on constructions where pressure/prohibition backfires into desire - 'makes food more desirable', 'urge to binge', 'pushed Ukraine into the arms of', 'I want to do it more', 'craving it more'. Positive pole fires on policy/economic harm verbs at ~10x smaller magnitude.

positive.read: Consequence nouns/verbs: ' intake', ' cut'/' cuts', 'TRILLION' fragment, ' crippled', 'assass' (assassinated), ' money' (lose gigantic sums), ' returns', ' tax', ' cancer' (HRT risk), ' keep' (keep more of their own money) - budget, sanctions and health-risk discourse.
evidence: act 3.20 'decreased energy [intake]... and weight loss' (d4186); 2.58 'effective [cut] in unemployment benefits' (d2407).
2.50 'lose gigantic sums of [money] every year' (d4073); 2.38 'increased the risk of breast [cancer]' (d594).

negative.read: ' desirable' (-25.8, 'forbidden...only makes food more desirable'), ' into'+' arms' ('pushed Ukraine into the arms of the West', -22.8/-22.5), ' binge'+' urge' (-19.5/-18.3), ' more' x2, ' craving', ' slows' (metabolism), ' over' (overeating), ' do it more'.
evidence: act -25.75 '"forbidden" only makes food more [desirable]; when your resistance breaks down' (d3686).
-22.75/-22.50 'Russia has pushed Ukraine [into] the [arms] of the West' (d1423); -19.88 'I want to do [it] more' (d2246).

caveats: The 'backfire-of-prohibition' frame is interpretive; 'pushed into the arms of' is geopolitical - the shared abstraction is 'pushed toward the opposed thing'.

validation: Minimal pairs: 'makes food more desirable' vs 'less desirable'; 'pushed into the arms of' vs 'pushed into talks with'.

positive.read: Positive pole fires almost exclusively on sentence-final '.' tokens, strongest as '.Ċ' (period + newline) closing list items or paragraphs in how-to/instructional documents (docs 2927, 2843, 814, 3789). Same surface token on both poles: the discriminative variable must be context, not token identity.

caveats: Both poles top out on '.' - a wrong-context control is essential to separate token identity from boundary context
Docs 2927, 814, 2843 exemplars repeat near-duplicate passages (template-driven docs)

Compare against random same-layer neurons and magnitude-matched controls

reads.summary: 31/32 negative exemplars are the token ' after'/'After' at acts -43.8 to -65.5 (' after' share 0.537, mass 0.616, lift 819x, eff 3.1). Positive pole is rare (15 sparse fires) and lands on tokens following before/after/following in temporal phrases.

positive.read: Complements of temporal connectives: ' a' ('After a real home business...'), ' Changing' ('after Changing some sheets'), ' any' ('following any such revisions'), ' topical' ('after topical application'), ' surgery' ('before surgery'), ' your' ('following your STOP request').
evidence: act 24.50 '.After a [real] home business' (d2173); 14.44 'entry-level after [Changing] some sheets' (d4730).
10.81 'following [any] amendment of these Terms' (d4243); 9.88 'as might be the case before [surgery]' (d2537).

negative.read: ' after' x26 + 'After' x5: idiom 'after all' (d2579, d3826, d2460, d918, d535), iteration 'one after another'/'book after book' (d861, d2854, d489, d1546), purposive 'players that are after exclusive gaming' (d3430).
evidence: act -65.50 'an eye on disbelief [after] a schleswig-holstein licence' (d428); -52.50 'it's a scam [after] all' (d2579); -46.50 'we are humans [after] all' (d918).
